text: It flips between pass and fail on unchanged firmware. Looking at one failing night (RUN-0034, Oct 4) to see where the slow answers come from.

**TC-DNS-005 is not a reliable test.** I classify it as a test issue, high confidence.

- On unchanged firmware 2.0.4 it failed 3 of the 8 nightly runs, with 6 verdict flips [[ev:RUN-0034/check/p95]]. By the test policy that is flaky [[ev:TB-01/doc/docs/test-policy.md#flaky-tests]].
- The DUT answers cached names in about 1 ms [[ev:RUN-0034/pcap/capture-lan/32]]. Every slow answer is a cache miss forwarded upstream: frame 3 took 31.8 ms on the LAN [[ev:RUN-0034/pcap/capture-lan/3]], and 31.0 ms of that was the upstream resolver's answer on the WAN [[ev:RUN-0034/pcap/capture-wan/2]]. The DUT adds under 1 ms.
- DNS-UP is a shared lab resolver whose latency varies with lab load [[ev:TB-01/doc/docs/lab-notes.md#2026-10-03]].

The p95 therefore measures the lab resolver, not the router. Recommendation: ticket to the test owner (qa-perf) to warm the cache before measuring, or to measure DUT-only latency (LAN answer time minus upstream time).
